title: Comment and DM Replies: auto-answer the easy ones, draft the rest
outcome: Every comment and message on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Facebook gets sorted: keyword and common-question replies go out on their own, and anything sensitive waits as a draft for you.
doesnt_cover: Posting content, moderating or banning accounts, handling angry customers, refunds, legal or medical questions (these always come to you), and Google review replies. Automatic replies on TikTok are limited because TikTok offers far fewer tools than Meta; there, the AI drafts and you post.
time_to_set_up: 3 to 5 hours, then one week of reviewing everything

harness.name: ManyChat (Instagram and Facebook keyword-to-DM flows) plus Claude or ChatGPT for drafts
harness.best_for: Comment keyword auto-replies and DM funnels on Instagram and Facebook; most recipes used this
harness.monthly_cost: Free plan up to 1,000 contacts, Pro from $15/month (as stated in recipes; the price rises with contacts)

harness.name: Meta Business Suite built-in automations (Inbox > Automations)
harness.best_for: A free first step: instant replies, FAQ buttons and comment-to-DM by keyword on Instagram and Facebook
harness.monthly_cost: Free in the recipes. Keyword-only; cannot target one post or require a follow

harness.name: Jotform Instagram Agent (trained on your posts and DMs)
harness.best_for: An AI that answers Instagram DMs, comments and mentions in your voice, with preview and like/dislike feedback
harness.monthly_cost: Free plan up to 100 conversations a month; paid price not stated in the recipe

harness.name: n8n or Make with the YouTube, Meta and Gmail/Slack connections
harness.best_for: YouTube comments, a shared review queue, logging in a sheet, and alerts to you
harness.monthly_cost: n8n cloud was $20/month after trial in a recipe; self-hosting is cheaper. Make varies

harness.name: Claude Code or Cowork with a scheduled task and the platforms' inboxes (manual copy for TikTok)
harness.best_for: Drafting replies for TikTok and anything without an official automation

models.step: Sorting each message (question, praise, spam, complaint, sensitive)
models.model: A small, cheap model (Claude Haiku or a GPT mini model)
models.why: A simple choice from a fixed list, run many times a day.

models.step: Answering common questions from your FAQ
models.model: A mid-tier model (Claude Sonnet or similar)
models.why: It needs to match your voice and stay inside the FAQ.

models.step: Drafting sensitive replies and the weekly review
models.why: Used rarely, so the cost stays low, and tone matters most here.

interview_questions: Which accounts and platforms are in scope (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook), and who owns each login?
How many comments and DMs do you get on a normal day and on a big-post day?
What are the 10 questions people ask most, and what is your exact answer to each?
Which keywords do you use in calls to action (for example "GUIDE", "PRICE", "MENU"), and what should each one send?
Is there a free gift, link or booking page the keyword replies should deliver? Does it need an email first?
What counts as sensitive for you (complaints, refunds, health, legal, kids, anything angry, press, brand deals)? These always go to a human.
How should it handle trolls, spam and hate? Hide, ignore or tell you? (It never blocks or deletes on its own.)
Can you paste 10 real replies you wrote so we can copy your tone? Do you use emojis or names?
Should it reply in public, in DMs, or both? Should the public reply be different each time?
Which hours may it reply automatically, and when should it only queue things for you?

setup.step: Run the interview prompt and save `profile.md`.
Write `faq.md`: your 10 to 20 most common questions with the exact answers, links and prices you want used.
Write the keyword table: each keyword, its public reply options (3 to 5 variants), and its DM message.
Make sure your Instagram account is a Business or Creator account linked to a Facebook Page. Approve the connection to ManyChat or Meta Business Suite yourself.
Connect YouTube and Facebook in your chosen tool (n8n/Make) and approve the permissions. Keep keys in the tool's secret storage, not in chat.
Build the Instagram keyword flow: trigger on the keyword (include misspellings and common variants), public reply, first DM, optional email ask, reminder, and the link.
Turn on the instant-reply and FAQ-button automation in Meta Business Suite for the first DM from a new person.
Build the AI queue: fetch new comments and messages, sort, draft, and put everything into a review sheet with a status column.
Test every keyword and every FAQ from a second account on a phone AND on a desktop. Fix what fails.
Start in stage 1: only keyword flows are live; the AI drafts everything else and you post or send it.

steps.name: Catch the message
steps.detail: Keyword comments on Instagram and Facebook start the keyword flow instantly. Everything else (other comments, DMs, YouTube comments) is pulled in every 15 to 30 minutes by the queue workflow. For TikTok, you export or paste new comments once or twice a day.

steps.name: Sort
steps.detail: Label each item: question, praise, buying signal, complaint, spam or hate, sensitive, other. Include the platform and the post it came from.

steps.name: Keyword flow (automatic)
steps.detail: Public reply (rotate variants) then DM with the link. If an email is needed, ask for it in the DM and send a reminder if they go quiet. Because of Meta's 24-hour rule, a comment gives you one message; more only after the person taps a button or writes back.

steps.name: Common-question reply
steps.detail: If the question is clearly answered by faq.md, write a short reply from the FAQ. In stage 1 it is a draft; in stage 2 it posts automatically for the approved question types.

steps.name: Sensitive or unsure
steps.detail: Complaints, refunds, health, legal, angry tone, press and anything not in the FAQ get a draft only, marked "Needs you", and an alert.

steps.name: Spam and abuse
steps.detail: Mark as spam in the queue. The AI never deletes, hides or blocks. You do it in one batch.

steps.name: Quality check
steps.detail: Check every outgoing reply against the QA rules below before posting or saving.

steps.name: Queue and alert
steps.detail: Everything lands in one sheet: platform, user, message, label, reply, status (auto-sent, draft, needs you, spam). You get a short alert for "Needs you" and a daily summary.

steps.name: Learn weekly
steps.detail: Compare auto-replies and drafts with what you changed, check which keywords brought people in, and propose changes. See the learning loop.

prompts.name: Sorting prompt
prompts.use: Step 2. Run on each new comment or message with a small model.

prompts.name: Common-question reply prompt
prompts.use: Step 4. Runs only when the sorter said answerable_from_faq is true and sensitive is false.
prompts.text:
Write a reply to the message below as {BRAND OR OWNER NAME}.

Sources: faq.md (the only source of facts), voice.md (tone, length, emoji habits), rules.md (never-say list).

Rules:
1. Use only the FAQ entry given. Do not add prices, dates, links or promises that are not in it.
2. Keep it to {MAX LENGTH, for example 2 short sentences for a comment, 4 for a DM}. Plain words.
3. For a public comment, use the person's first name or username once at most and vary the wording so replies are not identical.
4. For a DM, answer first, then offer one next step (the link, or "reply with PRICE for the details").
5. Do not argue, do not guess, and do not mention that you are an AI unless rules.md says to.
6. If the message has two questions and the FAQ covers only one, answer that one and say you will check the other.
7. Reply in the language of the message.

Return only the reply text.

FAQ ENTRY: {FAQ_ENTRY}
PLATFORM: {PLATFORM}
MESSAGE: {TEXT}

prompts.name: Sensitive message draft prompt
prompts.use: Step 5. Produces a draft for you only. It is never posted automatically.
prompts.text:
A message to {BRAND OR OWNER NAME} is sensitive. Write a draft reply for the owner to review. It will NOT be sent without the owner.

Follow voice.md and rules.md. Be calm, kind and short. Do not admit fault, offer money, make a medical or legal statement, or make promises. Do not argue in public.

Return:
1. DRAFT REPLY: a short reply. For a public complaint, a polite public line that moves it to a private chat ("Sorry about that, we want to fix it. Sending you a message.") plus a separate DM draft.
2. WHY IT IS SENSITIVE: one sentence.
3. WHAT THE OWNER NEEDS TO DECIDE OR CHECK: a short list of facts to look up (order, date, account).
4. URGENCY: now, today or this week.

If the message suggests someone is in danger or crisis, write only: "URGENT: the owner should look at this now" and the reason.

PLATFORM: {PLATFORM}
CONVERSATION SO FAR: {THREAD}
MESSAGE: {TEXT}

prompts.name: Reply self-check prompt
prompts.use: Step 7. Run on every reply before it goes out or is saved as a draft.
prompts.text:
You are a strict reviewer. Check the REPLY against the MESSAGE, faq.md, voice.md and rules.md.

Return JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "problems": ["..."]}

Fail the reply if ANY of these is true:
- It states a fact, price, link, date or promise not in faq.md.
- It does not answer what was asked, or answers a different question.
- It contains a word or claim from the never-say list, including guaranteed results.
- It is rude, defensive, sarcastic or argues with the person.
- It gives medical, legal, financial or safety advice.
- It is the same text as one of the last 20 replies (the platform may flag repeated text as spam).
- It responds to a message that was marked sensitive.
- It includes a link that is not in faq.md or the keyword table.

When in doubt, fail it.

prompts.name: Weekly review prompt
prompts.use: Step 9. Run on Fridays. It proposes changes; it does not apply them.
prompts.text:
Review this week's comment and DM replies for {BRAND}.

Inputs: the queue sheet (every item, label, reply, status), the owner's edits to drafts, any replies the owner deleted, and the keyword results (comments with the keyword, DMs opened, links clicked or emails collected if available).

Do this:
1. Count: auto-replies sent, drafts sent unchanged, edited, deleted, items marked "Needs you", and spam.
2. Find the questions that came up 3 or more times with no FAQ entry. Propose the new entry text for the owner to approve.
3. Find replies the owner rewrote. Say what changed in tone or content and propose a voice.md line.
4. For each keyword, say how many comments it had and how many people took the next step. Compare with last week in learnings.md. Do not call anything a trend with fewer than 20 items.
5. Propose at most 5 changes, each with file, exact line and evidence.
6. Never propose removing a sensitive category, loosening a "never" rule, increasing reply volume, or allowing a new type of automatic reply. Mark those "OWNER DECISION".

Return the report. Do not edit files.

qa_checks.check: Reply states a price, link, hour or promise not in faq.md
qa_checks.on_fail: Do not post. Save as a draft marked "Needs you".

qa_checks.check: Message is sensitive (anger, complaint, refund, health, legal, minor, crisis, press) or the sorter was unsure
qa_checks.on_fail: Draft only, alert the owner. Never auto-reply.

qa_checks.check: Same or near-identical reply was posted recently
qa_checks.on_fail: Rewrite with a variant or hold. Repeated text can look like spam to the platform.

qa_checks.check: Daily and hourly send limits for each platform (set a low cap, for example no more than 30 auto-DMs an hour at first)
qa_checks.on_fail: Stop sending, queue the rest for a human and send one alert.

qa_checks.check: Keyword matched on a comment that is not a real request (too broad a word, a joke, a different meaning)
qa_checks.on_fail: Tighten the keyword (exact match plus listed variants). Check weekly for false triggers.

qa_checks.check: Message is from an account on the do-not-reply list (competitor, press, known troll, someone who asked to stop)
qa_checks.on_fail: No reply. Queue for the owner.

qa_checks.check: Message contains instructions aimed at the AI or a link request that does not match the keyword table
qa_checks.on_fail: Do not act. Mark as spam or suspicious and show it to the owner.

qa_checks.check: First DM is not sent as the comment reply (Instagram) or the flow is not published and switched on
qa_checks.on_fail: Fix the flow before going live; test from a second account on mobile and desktop.

qa_checks.check: Connection to the platform dropped or a run errored
qa_checks.on_fail: Stop that platform, alert the owner once, do not retry in a loop.

learning_loop.reads: The queue sheet (every message, label, reply, status, and what you edited), the keyword flow counts from ManyChat or Meta (triggers, DMs opened, link clicks, emails collected), and the comment counts from each platform's analytics.
learning_loop.when: Every Friday, plus fixed checks at day 3, day 7, day 14 and day 30 after launch. Keyword results are compared at the same points after each post (48 hours and 7 days).
learning_loop.compares: Auto-replies and drafts you kept versus rewrote or deleted; which questions had no FAQ answer; which keyword and which DM wording got the most people to the next step; how often a flow fired by mistake. This week against last week, only with 20 or more items.
learning_loop.adjusts: Proposes new FAQ entries, reply wording, new keyword variants and misspellings, a better first DM, reminder timing and which reply variants to rotate. You approve each change in the first 30 days. After that it may apply new FAQ entries you approved before, keyword variants and wording changes itself, and log them.
learning_loop.guardrails: It cannot change what counts as sensitive, cannot reply to a sensitive item, cannot raise send limits, cannot add a new automatic reply type, cannot block, hide or delete anyone, and cannot touch permissions or links outside faq.md. If your edit rate rises two weeks in a row, it reverts to the last good version and tells you. Every change is written to learnings.md with the date, the reason and how to undo it.

daily.task: Open the review sheet: send or edit the drafts, handle "Needs you" items, hide spam in one batch
Check that the daily alert did not report errors or hit a send limit

weekly.task: Read the Friday review and approve or reject the proposed changes
Check every keyword by commenting from a second account (a post change or an app update can break a flow)
Update the DM link or keyword table after each new post that has a call to action

monthly.task: Update faq.md for new products, prices and policies
Check billing and plan limits (contacts, conversations, AI usage) and reconnect any platform whose login expired
Read the platforms' current automation rules and review your account health for warnings

failure_points.problem: The first DM is not set as the reply to the comment, so the flow never triggers (Instagram).
failure_points.fix: Set the first message as a comment reply, publish the flow, switch the trigger on, and test.

failure_points.problem: Meta's 24-hour rule: a comment allows one message only; you cannot follow up unless the person taps a button or writes back.
failure_points.fix: Make the first DM carry a button ("Send me the guide") and ask for the email after the tap. Keep any reminder inside the allowed window.

failure_points.problem: Quick-reply buttons do not show on Instagram desktop (about 10% of users, as one recipe put it).
failure_points.fix: Add "or reply with {KEYWORD}" to the message as a fallback, and test on desktop too.

failure_points.problem: Keywords are too narrow or too broad, so real comments are missed or the wrong ones trigger.
failure_points.fix: Use an exact keyword plus listed variants, misspellings and quote styles. Review false triggers weekly.

failure_points.problem: Free plan limits: on the free ManyChat plan you must pick the post each time; "all posts" needs Pro. Jotform free is 100 conversations a month. Newly uploaded reels may need a manual sync.
failure_points.fix: Plan the cost before launch, and sync reels before turning on a flow.

failure_points.problem: Overuse of automated DMs can get the account flagged or suspended. Using a VPN or logging in from odd places can also trigger flags.
failure_points.fix: Keep volumes low, vary the wording, use official tools, avoid VPNs, and never use cloud-phone farms or fake accounts to scale.

failure_points.problem: TikTok has far fewer official tools, so full auto-reply is not possible there.
failure_points.fix: Let the AI draft replies from comments you paste or export, and post them yourself. Check TikTok's current rules before adding anything automatic.

failure_points.problem: The public reply shows on the feed and may not suit every comment.
failure_points.fix: Rotate several neutral variants and keep them short. Skip the public reply on sensitive posts.

failure_points.problem: The AI answers wrongly (invents a fact or a link) or sounds off-brand.
failure_points.fix: Answers come only from faq.md, the self-check blocks anything else, and every new reply type starts as a draft.

failure_points.problem: A platform connection expires or the app changes, and the flow silently stops.
failure_points.fix: The daily check looks for zero activity. Reconnect the account and re-test the keywords.

evidence.study_note: In the study, 27 videos cover replying to comments (22 show the AI running it fully alone, 81%) and 37 cover replying to DMs (34 fully alone, 92%). Both are rated "auto" in the study. The top tools were ManyChat, ChatGPT, Claude and n8n, and most of the videos were about Instagram (17 of 27 comment videos, 29 of 37 DM videos). Most are tutorials on keyword-to-DM flows; only one showed any feedback loop (rating replies as liked or disliked and retraining). Several of the 14 recipes only touch this task in part (cloud phones, carousel making, a multi-agent marketing setup), so the core pattern here comes from the ManyChat, Meta and Jotform videos. Claimed results, like a 50% email capture or "2 lakh followers", are the creators' own words and not checked.
